messages:

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Security exhibit runbook + proposed evidence cadence for Order Form

Hi Jorge / Lumina security team —

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. As discussed on the demo, we want to keep the commercial paperwork moving while we align on the security exhibit (SOC 2 scope and pen-test window). Attached is a concise runbook that proposes:

- A 4-week evidence cadence for SOC 2 list items we already have artifacts for.
- A 2-week staging window for the pen-test and a separate 48-hour on-call for log access.
- An SLA-exception path when customers request broader inspection rights (proposal below).

Could you confirm:
1) Which SOC 2 assertions you need validated (PII/SSO/Logging/Encryption)?
2) Whether Lumina requires any site-inspection window vs. privileged inspection?
3) Who on your side will own the procurement checklist?

Attachments: Lumina_Security_Questions_v2.xlsx (you sent this during the call), runbook-audit-rights-draft.md

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min handoff with legal and infra ops tomorrow.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Monica —

Appreciate the draft. A few clarifying points from our security team:

- Lumina needs confirmation that SOC 2 scope covers data-at-rest encryption and key management (we list KM and HSM in our vendor policy). Please call out KMS/HSM details.
- For pen-testing, we require a 72-hour staging window and a single 4-hour privileged-access session for evidence review; can Redwood support that?
- We would like the evidence cadence to include a snapshot of access logs for the prior 90 days for scoped resources.

I'll attach a short markup to your Excel and mark the high-priority asks. Suggest we lock technical points this week and legal can do redlines next.

Monica — copying quick notes for legal ops and next steps before we reply to Lumina: 

- KMS/HSM: our private deployments support customer-managed KMS via Cloud KMS and HSM integrations; we should add a one-line statement and link to the KMS appendix, not expose internal key material.
- Pen-test window: engineering prefers 48–72 hrs; dev ops flagged the 4-hour live privileged session as fine if done via jumpbox and recorded.
- 90-day logs: we can provide aggregated access logs and sampling; full log exports are treated as privileged evidence and need a signed inspection playbook.

Action items: 
1) Karthik — can you prepare a short technical note (<=1 page) on KMS/HSM integration and jumpbox workflow? Needed by EOD.
2) Aditya — I can draft an SLA-exception path that punts to CSM/legal for any full-log exports.
3) Monica — propose the 72-hour pen-test window and 4-hour session to Lumina and ask for the owner for procurement.

I'll keep this tight; legal will want to review redlines to the MSA/order form once Lumina returns comments.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Laura / Monica —

Attached is the one-page tech note and the suggested language we can insert into the security exhibit. High level:

- Key management: support for customer-managed KMS via Cloud KMS; when customer requests HSM-backed keys we surface an integration path — we WILL NOT export private key material. Suggested clause: "Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; Redwood will provide connector configuration and audit logs; private key material remains under customer control."
- Pen-test process: recommend phrasing: "Pen-test windows: Customer may schedule a staging window (minimum 72 hours). Privileged review sessions limited to a single scheduled 4-hour session via Redwood-provided jumpbox, recorded and view-only to Redwood personnel unless otherwise agreed."
- Logs: we can provide 90-day aggregated access logs; full raw log exports require an inspection playbook and executed NDA + limited-scope inspection.

I've attached Draft_MSA_redlines_20261215.pdf with inline suggestions for the exhibit and a separate short runbook section.

Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: J. Morales <jmorales@luminadx.com>, security@luminadx.com, procurement@luminadx.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit runbook + proposed evidence cadence for Order Form — proposed final path

Jorge — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed internally and propose the following consolidated path so legal can move to redlines:

1) SOC 2 scope: Call out data-at-rest encryption and KMS/HSM support (we will not surface private key material).
2) Pen-test: 72-hour staging window; one 4-hour privileged access session via Redwood jumpbox (recorded).
3) Logs: provide 90-day aggregated access logs as standard. Full raw log exports are considered privileged evidence and will require execution of an inspection playbook + signed addendum (SLA-exception path below).

SLA-exception path (when customer requests raw logs or on-site inspection):
- Step A: Customer raises request via procurement and security (Lumina).
- Step B: Redwood CS and Legal evaluate; if accepted, we run a 2-week technical onboarding and require an executed inspection addendum (NDA + limited-scope).
- Step C: Execution window and costs: we propose a one-time professional services fee for privileged evidence handling; any additional time is billed.

Next step: if Lumina agrees to the high-level path, we'll circulate Draft_MSA_redlines_20261215.pdf to legal and route for redline consolidation. Could you confirm procurement owner so we can loop legal?

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
